title: Plant shutdown chronology
prompt: Create one complete 16:9 documentary image for CAMP CENTURY. Image1 establishes the OWNER-APPROVED DRAWING STYLE ONLY: confident detailed ink and charcoal linework, restrained watercolor, paper tooth, blue-white snow, olive winter clothes, sparse rusty ochre objects. Do not copy its composition or subjects unless requested. Any additional image is FACT reference only. Match the drawing style, not a new design system. Full finished composition, large explanatory drawing, legible short English labels integrated into the scene/paper. A full illustrated historical chronology document on natural paper, with three connected charcoal-and-watercolor scenes across the page: a quiet plant doorway, generic machinery being lifted onto a sled, and a snow-covered abandoned surface entrance. The plant is an ordinary period installation, no technical internals. Integrate three clear headings and short explanatory lines: JULY 1963 / Plant shut down; 1964 / Plant hardware removed; LATER 1960s / Seasonal work ended. Do not invent a single exact last-occupation date, explosion, collapse or contaminated plume. Drawing fills the frame, readable captions embedded beneath their own scene. All base artwork must be CLEAN: NO yellow highlighting, NO underlines, NO marker strokes, NO selection circles, NO loupes, NO glow or animated accents baked into the image; those are added later in DaVinci Resolve. No generic three-line title card, UI, HUD, floating boxes, fake official seals/signatures/stamps, tiny filler text, placeholders, empty panels, decorative noise or burnt parchment. Use 6 percent safe margins. This is authored explanatory artwork, not an original archival record. No invented quantities, dimensions or measurement curves. No other projects or bases. Text only as explicitly specified.
